audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart on this page is [Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, Sion, Sion] in BOTH layers. The packet chart is [Sion, Sion, Skill, Skill, Kayle, Kayle, Kayle], and the mirrored kayle__sion audit states it aligned its chart to the packet.
audit.why: The page's own prose already contradicts its chart: whys[5] says 'she wins this trade' while win[5] said Sion, and whys[6] says she 'scales harder than any HP juggernaut can match' while win[6] said Sion. A 48.51% win rate over 1713 games with a Nashor's on-hit scaler is a losing late game, not a winning one. The packet chart is the correct one and the mirror is already on it.
audit.corrected: Rows flipped in matched pairs across both layers: L1 Sion, L2 Sion, L3 Skill, L4-5 Skill, L6 Kayle, 1st item Kayle, 2+ items Kayle.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.phases[5].why calls first item 'your spike - force fights', and phases[1].why tells you to trade at Level 2 'when Kayle's Divine Judgment is down'.
audit.why: Divine Judgment does not exist until level 6, so a Level 2 instruction to track it is unusable. And the first-item window belongs to Kayle here, not Sion: Nashor's-style on-hit scales off the HP Heartsteel just bought you.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why now points at her having no dash and no R yet; phases[5] and phases[6] now read as Kayle windows. Divine Judgment's rank-1 cooldown of 160s is now stated so 'bait it' is a countable window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit interactions the page never mentions: Celestial Blessing's heal and Starfire Spellblade's auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Brief flags both. Celestial Blessing is a flat 15s heal on herself and the nearest ally, which undoes exactly the chip-damage grind Sion plays for — Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades. Starfire Spellblade is a 6-8s auto reset dealing bonus damage proportionate to MISSING health, so her burst tell is the attack wind-up and it is at its worst when you are already low.
audit.corrected: Both written into mid, with the anti-heal purchase timed before the second item.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects flags 'Her Divine Judgment' as a probable wrong name.
audit.why: False positive — Divine Judgment is the correct name of Kayle's R in the kit file. No rename made.

edits.after: Divine Judgment answers your charged Q all-in outright — but it is 160s at rank 1, so a baited R hands you the whole lane until it comes back.

edits.after: Divine Judgment arrives at 6 on a 160s cooldown — bait it with a W-pop, then commit the charged Q; if she spends it, the lane is yours again.

edits.before: At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Kayle now has Divine Judgment, and she will hold it as a get-out the instant you open a charged Q animation. Bait the R first — pop your W-shield into her to force an early shield pop or make her burn R defensively, then follow with Q-E the moment it expires. Do not dump your full all-in while her R is up or you hand her a free lane reset. Her ranged form waveclear also starts to come online around level 6; respect her auto damage and avoid trading when you are at half HP with no W-shield available.
edits.after: At level 6 the dynamic shifts: Kayle now has Divine Judgment, and she will hold it as a get-out the instant you open a charged Q animation. It is 160s at rank 1 — bait it, then run Q-E while it is gone. Do not dump your all-in while her R is up or you hand her a free lane reset. Celestial Blessing heals her every 15s flat, so buy Grievous Wounds before your second item or your chip damage is refunded. Watch her attack wind-up, not her casts: Starfire Spellblade is a 6-8s auto reset that scales with your missing health, so it hits hardest exactly when you are low.

notes: The level chart was wrong on both layers at once — it read as a Sion late game against a 48.51% win rate and against the page's own text, which twice says Kayle wins the scaling. I flipped five rows as matched full/content pairs and left the two rows the packet already agreed with. Ratings left untouched: their scale is not documented in the brief and guessing at it risks a second inconsistency. Note the full layer for this matchup contains mojibake (em dashes stored as 'a EUR"'); I copied the before-strings byte-for-byte from the brief and used plain hyphens in my replacements rather than reintroducing the broken sequence. That encoding damage is champion-wide in the full file and is worth a separate pass.
